0.expectation: An isolated otelcol-contrib 0.161.0 running the repository collector.yaml privacy processors unchanged (ports rewritten, live-probe pipelines dropped) plus isolated Prometheus 3.14.0 and Loki 3.7.8 will drop synthetic canary secrets placed in every non-allowlisted log/metric/resource/scope field, and the positive control (a canary in an allowlisted attribute) will appear, proving the query paths can detect a leak.
0.criteria: Script exits 0 only if (a) each canary sent through a non-allowlisted field is absent from Prometheus (series + label values), Loki (query_range over the fixture window, all structured metadata) and the file/events receipt file, and (b) the allowlisted-field positive control is found in each backend where that field is exported. A detection self-test (the same script run against a pass-through collector config) must report leaks and exit non-zero. Any leak in the privacy run = fail.

1.expectation: A script can run one bounded native Claude -p task against an isolated collector/Prometheus pair and reproduce per-category equality between the stream-json result usage and the Prometheus counter delta for input, output, cacheRead and cacheCreation.
1.criteria: Script exists under blueprints/, runs exactly one claude -p call (bounded max-turns, no tools, no MCP, hooks disabled, user settings not loaded so telemetry goes only to the isolated collector), captures before and after Prometheus snapshots, and prints a per-category comparison. Pass = every category's delta equals the native result usage; mismatch or missing series is reported as such, not coerced.

2.expectation: Enabling a scheduled user unit, daemon-reload/restart of the live user manager and a host-wide wsl --shutdown are outside this unit's isolation rules and would interrupt peer sessions; an isolated systemd user manager is not expected to be startable in an unprivileged namespace here.
2.criteria: Try whether an isolated alternative (unshare user/pid/mount namespace with a private systemd --user instance) can host a timer; if it cannot, record the exact blocker and defer. Settled would need a fired timer across daemon-reload and restart plus a post-wsl---shutdown check_persistence.py pass.

3.expectation: With an isolated collector/Prometheus pair receiving telemetry only from the single child Claude process, the before snapshot will be empty and the after-minus-before delta per category will equal the native result usage; an attribution side pipeline will show exactly one session.id equal to the --session-id passed to the child.
3.criteria: Pass = before snapshot has no ecosystem_claude_code_token_usage_tokens_total series; after snapshot per type equals the child's stream-json usage; the attribution file shows only the child's session.id. Live Prometheus is queried read-only for that session's absence as a leak detector (the repo pipeline strips session.id, so detection there uses a fresh-series check limited to what is observable).

4.expectation: Inside an unprivileged user+mount namespace, a size-limited tmpfs spool (e.g. 256 KiB) will fill; the SDK receipt writer will fail atomically on ENOSPC without partial files; with the collector stopped for an extended interval and later restarted, file_log will replay every complete receipt into an isolated Loki with no duplicates; an added expiry policy script will delete only receipts older than the TTL whose ingestion is confirmed.
4.criteria: Count: receipts attempted, receipts written, ENOSPC refusals, partial files (must be 0), receipts in Loki after restore (must equal written, distinct receipt_id), duplicates (must be 0). Expiry policy test: unit tests plus a run on the tmpfs spool that frees space and allows new writes. Extended interval = at least 3 minutes collector down and Loki down for part of it.

5.expectation: Jaeger 2.21.0 (checksum-verified, loopback, in-memory storage) will accept OTLP traces from one ephemeral codex exec session configured with a trace_exporter override, and the Jaeger query API will return that trace by its ID.
5.criteria: Pass = at least one trace with service codex_exec (or the native service name) found via /api/v3/traces or /api/traces search, then fetched again by trace ID with span count > 0. Record which spans/attributes exist and whether content leaks. Live pipeline stays trace-disabled (not changed).

6.expectation: Firing N=20 distinct synthetic alerts through an isolated Alertmanager 0.34.1 using the repository route (group_wait 5s) into an isolated ntfy 2.28.0 with the repository alertmanager template will give an end-to-end latency near group_wait (about 5 s) with small spread.
6.criteria: Report min/median/p90/max of (ntfy stream arrival time - alert POST time) over N alerts, count delivered/lost. Pass = all N delivered and a distribution recorded; the number itself is not pass/fail.

2.expectation: Uncertain. This process sits in the root-owned /init.scope cgroup, so a private systemd --user in an unprivileged user+pid+mount namespace may fail to set up cgroups; if it starts, the pipeline timer settings (OnBootSec=45s, OnUnitActiveSec=2min, AccuracySec=10s, copied verbatim; service replaced by a harmless marker-file append) fire before and after a daemon-reload and after a manager restart.
2.criteria: Harness: unshare --user --map-root-user --pid --fork --mount-proc --mount; tmpfs over /run/user/1000 so the live manager socket is unreachable; temp HOME/XDG_*; SYSTEMD_UNIT_PATH set to a temp dir only; DBUS_SESSION_BUS_ADDRESS unset; enable the timer with systemctl --user enable against the private manager. Detection: each service run appends a UTC timestamp to a marker file; a phase counts as fired only if a new marker line appears after the event (daemon-reload; manager SIGTERM + restart with the same unit dir) within 180 s. If the manager cannot start or cannot run the service, record its exact stderr/exit as the blocker for these arms. Outcome stays advanced regardless: this is a local_integration check of timer semantics on a private manager; the live-manager and wsl --shutdown + check_persistence.py arms stay open. Time-box 20 min.

addendum.label: addendum written after attempt 1 (14:19:04Z) and the strace diagnosis (14:21:01Z), before attempt 2
addendum.observed_blocker: private systemd --user exits 1 after openat(/sys/fs/cgroup/init.scope/cgroup.procs) = EACCES: the caller sits in the root-owned /init.scope cgroup (its log target /dev/console is also EACCES, hence no message).
addendum.plan: Attempt 2 runs the same harness inside the project-sanctioned $HOME/codex-ecosystem/bin/ecosystem-bounded-run, whose transient scope under the live user manager is owned by uid 1000 (ECOSYSTEM_JOB_SECONDS=1100). This creates one transient scope on the live user manager, as every bounded job here does; no unit file, reload or restart of the live manager.
addendum.criteria: Unchanged from fix_round_3.gaps.2. If the manager still cannot start, the exact failing syscall/stderr is the recorded blocker.

addendum_2.label: second addendum, written after attempt 2 (14:21:35-14:39:55Z) and before attempt 3
addendum_2.observed: Attempt 2: the private manager started (state=running) inside the bounded scope and the timer was enabled and active, but no marker line appeared in 180 s; after daemon-reload the timer showed ActiveState=failed; SIGTERM did not stop the manager (no exit.target in the private unit path), so the harness hung until its 1100 s timeout (exit 143). The manager log was empty because it logs to /dev/console (EACCES).
addendum_2.plan: Attempt 3 = same harness plus: /dev/console bind-mounted to a temp file inside the private mount namespace so the manager log is kept; a private exit.target (DefaultDependencies=no, SuccessAction=exit-force) so SIGTERM exits the manager, with a 30 s bound then SIGKILL (recorded); systemctl --user show/status of the service and timer after each phase. Diagnostic of the same criteria; they are unchanged.
addendum_2.criteria: Unchanged from fix_round_3.gaps.2. If the stand-in service still does not run, the manager log line that explains it is the recorded blocker.

addendum_3.label: third addendum, written after attempt 3 (14:43:19-14:46:40Z) and before attempt 4
addendum_3.observed: Attempt 3: manager running, SIGTERM bound in place, but the timer went to ActiveState=failed about 40 s after start while the stand-in service never ran (Result=success, ExecMainCode=0, inactive); /dev/console bind produced no log lines. Operator stopped attempt 3 at 14:46:40Z by SIGKILL of the namespace init after an over-broad pkill -f also matched the operator shell.
addendum_3.hypothesis: The private unit path lacked basic.target, which user services require through default dependencies, so the timer could not queue the service start job.
addendum_3.plan: Attempt 4 = attempt 3 plus stock basic.target, sockets.target, paths.target and shutdown.target copied verbatim from /usr/lib/systemd/user (unit files only, no .wants directories), and the timer Result property in each state line.
addendum_3.criteria: Unchanged from fix_round_3.gaps.2. If the service still does not run, record the timer Result and stop; the arms stay open.
